doc.title: Frank Strazzeri interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Favorite recent albums
summary: He recalls the album with John Patitucci and a Chet trio album.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You’ve got some fascinating stuff there, from all your jazz to Elvis to Chet Baker. What is a recent album that you’re really happy with? Is there a recent album you’ve done that you’re really happy with? One of these? You can’t remember the titles, right?
No I remember titles, no I don’t remember the titles no. Did I do something wrong here with this?
We just lost — just clip it back on.

Well this is like a group, one thing. I don’t know. I sort of like this. Yeah, “Can Dancing,” yeah that was a good album, John Patatucci. This is the first, I think the first jazz — he did this with me just before he joined Chick Corea. Absolutely. When we finished this, the very day we finished it, he left and he went to Chick Corea’s house to join him. He went to rehearse. Nice kid too. A nice album. I guess I’d have to say this is one of the nicer things that I probably did, solo piano thing. I don’t know if it’s even © Fillius Jazz Archive -21-
around anymore. These kind of things are — let’s see I did this thing for Chet. This probably is one of the better things I did, a trio thing.
